newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Britomart developers plan NZ$50mln public issue.
newsitem.headline: NZ Britomart developers plan NZ$50mln public issue.

text.p: The developers of Auckland's Britomart complex, Pacific Capital Assets, are planning a NZ$50 million public issue as part of a possible sharemarket listing, the New Zealand Herald reported on Friday.
Brokers have already been approached for possible interest in an issue. The timing of the float, if it proceeds, would likely be within the next three to six months.

With funding already finalised for the initial NZ$350 million transport centre development, the proceeds from the float would be used for further infrastructure developments in Australia and New Zealand.
But part of the aim is to get public participation in the controversial project.
The Herald reported that after months of heated debate, the project was awaiting final resource consents. The developers hope to start the project in the latter part of this year.
The Herald said it was believed the listed vehicle would have shareholders' funds of around NZ$150 million, including the public pool.
The Britomart project is estimated to cost NZ$1.5 billion, including above-ground development of medium-rise apartments, commercial offices, hotels and shops.
Funding for the first stage development is from an Australian subsidiary of the National Westminster Bank.
It will provide up to NZ$300 million for the project, with the balance put in by Pacific Capital.

The owners of Pacific Capital are mainly Asian based. Its largest single investor is Hudson Corporate, a wholly owned unit of Australia's Hudson Timber and Hardware, whose major shareholders are from Singapore and Malaysia.
